labels.name: Scale
labels.function: Surface flaking that makes MF lesions look like eczema or psoriasis

labels.name: Epidermis
labels.function: Layer the malignant cells percolate into in early lesions

labels.name: Pautrier microabscess
labels.function: Small intraepidermal cluster of lymphoma cells (not neutrophils)

labels.name: Epidermotropism
labels.function: Single malignant cells extending up among keratinocytes

labels.name: Upper dermal infiltrate
labels.function: Patch-stage collection of atypical lymphocytes just below epidermis

labels.name: Diffuse dermal infiltrate
labels.function: Larger, sheet-like spread of lymphoma cells in plaques and tumors

labels.name: Cerebriform nucleus
labels.function: Folded outline like brain sulci and gyri; hallmark of MF cells

labels.name: Sezary cell
labels.function: Malignant T cell once in the circulation; >1000/mL in leukemic disease

labels.name: Patch
labels.function: Flat, scaly lesion; earliest stage, often misdiagnosed as eczema

labels.name: Plaque
labels.function: Raised, thick scaly lesion; more advanced, may mimic psoriasis

labels.name: Tumor
labels.function: Nodule of lymphoma cells; treated with radiation

labels.name: Erythroderma
labels.function: Red scale over the entire skin surface; causes chills

labels.name: Lymphadenopathy
labels.function: Enlarged nodes of advanced disease; assessed in staging

labels.name: Splenomegaly
labels.function: Organ enlargement seen on CT in advanced disease

labels.name: Sezary cell
labels.function: Malignant T cell in blood; defines the leukemic form
